Hildegard 0.1.1 is a pre-alpha. It fixes what a full test of 0.1.0 found on Windows, macOS, Linux, WSL2 and Omarchy.

## Install

- **macOS and Linux:** `curl -fsSL https://dbaney.com/hildegard/install.sh | sh`
- **Windows (PowerShell):** `irm https://dbaney.com/hildegard/install.ps1 | iex`
- **Desktop app:** pick your system's download below, or from [dbaney.com/hildegard](https://dbaney.com/hildegard/).

## Fixed

- **Windows:**
  - The installers check free space before downloading anything. When there isn't enough room, they print the exact command to install on another drive.
  - Installing to an exFAT or FAT32 drive now works. Before, unpacking, the `app` link and uv's Python each failed on such a drive.
  - uv's download cache stays in Hildegard's folder instead of filling C:.
  - `hildegard start` over ssh no longer stops the server when the session closes.
- **Every system:** the server stays up when the terminal that started it closes, and its log says why it stopped.
- **macOS:** the disk image opens without a license prompt, and the app's signature is valid. The app isn't notarized yet: the first time you open it, choose **Open Anyway** in System Settings › Privacy & Security.
- **Desktop app:** it now uses an existing install wherever its `hildegard` command points, instead of offering to install a second copy.
- **Doctor on a Mac:** it now points you to pairing a GPU computer, and stops asking for a Hugging Face account a Mac can't use.
- **Paired renders:** a take's render time no longer counts its wait in the GPU computer's queue.

## Known limits

- Macs don't render on their own GPU yet. Pair a Mac with a computer that has an NVIDIA or AMD GPU
  (`hildegard choir join`).
- The Windows and macOS apps aren't code-signed yet, so Windows SmartScreen and macOS Gatekeeper ask you to confirm the first launch.
- LTX models follow Lightricks' license: free under $10M yearly revenue, and not for products that compete with
  Lightricks. Wan 2.2 is Apache-2.0.
